key_insight: Fermion-to-qubit encodings are not just translation tools: they induce meaningful geometric structure, captured via hypergraph connectivity and coupling-space transport, that reveals new organization in encoded Hamiltonians.
engineering_relevance: This provides quantum algorithm designers with geometry-based diagnostics for comparing encodings and understanding how interaction structure propagates into qubit Hamiltonians, which can inform mapping choice and simulation efficiency.
method: Built weighted hypergraph representations for Bravyi–Kitaev (BK) and Xia–Bian–Kais (XBK) encodings.
Defined a BK geometric observable comparing kinetic vs interaction hypergraph connectivity and derived its exact dependence on interaction strength.
Used probability measures and optimal transport in XBK coupling space to quantify interaction-driven reorganization independently of spectral analysis.
evidence_signal: The framework is demonstrated on the Hubbard, spinless tV, single-impurity Anderson, and Kitaev models, showing consistent structural changes across distinct many-body systems.
watch_item: The results are representation-dependent and rely on exact encoding structure, so extending the geometric diagnostics to noisy, approximate, or hardware-constrained encodings may require additional validation.
paper_title: A Geometric Theory of Fermion-to-Qubit Encodings
